subject: One-time onboarding buydown credit request for NexaHealth - VP/CFO approval needed
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: One-time buydown credit ask for NexaHealth (urgent)

Ben / Marissa —

Quick summary: NexaHealth is ready to sign a 24-month committed contract (expected ARR ~ $1.1M) but procurement is pushing for a vendor-side "buydown" credit to offset first-year implementation costs and a third-party integration. They view this as a gating item for their November board approval window.

What I'm asking: VP/CFO sign-off for a one-time, front-loaded credit equal to 8% of first-year committed spend (approx $88k). In return, we get a locked 24-month term, auto-renew with 12% step-up in year 2, and a minimum monthly usage floor to avoid churn risk.

Rationale / mitigants:
- High expansion potential in their provider network (they run trials across 12 hospitals).
- Customer will sign our standard MSS + bring their own KMS; security team cleared the baseline.
- We will include a firm MAC (minimum annual commitment) clause and a 9-month non-cancel buyout to protect economics.

Attachments: pricing_model_buydown.xlsx (breaks down token economics), SOW_NexaHealth_v2.pdf, mutual_action_plan.docx

If this needs to be routed as a formal exception memo to Finance/Legal, I can draft a short note for Markus to sign. Need a decision by EOD Monday — their procurement has a wishlist to the board on Tuesday morning.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: One-time buydown credit ask for NexaHealth (urgent)

Tessa —

Appreciate the context. Two quick suggestions before we escalate to Markus formally:

1) Reduce the upfront credit to 6% if we can secure an explicit expansion guarantee: they commit to a pilot-to-prod rollout across at least 4 hospitals in first 12 months and provide a named list of expansion targets.
2) Add a performance milestone: 50% of the credit is clawed back if they fail to hit usage floor after month 9.

I'll be fine if Markus signs off on a conditional 6% with those guardrails. If Finance needs the 8% ask, include a short numbered memo that outlines the upside and clawback language — one page. Happy to help draft.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Reviewed the attached model. A few finance notes:
- 8% is on the high side given our historical concession bands for similar-sized POC->enterprise deals. 6% with strong clawback and an explicit step-up is acceptable.
- Require a contract amendment template that enumerates clawback triggers, timing, and calculation methodology. Legal will need to review the MAC language you mentioned.
- Please confirm that the implementation vendor contribution (they expect a $20k pass-through) is captured separately in the SOW; we should not gross that against our credit.

If you can update the model to 6% and add the 50% milestone/9-month clawback Ben suggested, Finance is likely to clear. I can prepare the exception memo for Markus to sign (one page, finance justification + ROI table).

Subject: Re: One-time buydown credit ask for NexaHealth (urgent)

Team —

Thanks for the clear write-ups. I'm prepared to approve a conditional 6% one-time buydown credit with the following mandatory conditions:

1) Expansion clause: NexaHealth must commit to a 24-month term with a minimum annual usage floor and an explicit list of four hospitals targeted for production within 12 months.
2) Clawback: 50% of the credit is repayable if usage floor is not met by the end of month 9; repayment schedule: net-off against future invoices across the remainder of year one.
3) Implementation vendor pass-through: confirm in SOW that the $20k integration pass-through is billed separately and is not considered part of Redwood's gross ARR for the credit calculation.
4) Legal signoff on the amendment language and Finance (Marissa) to prepare the one-page exception memo.

Tessa — please prepare the signed exception memo and updated pricing model reflecting 6% plus the clawback mechanics. Once I have the memo and clean SOW showing the pass-through, I will authorize Markus Klein (VP, Finance) signature.

Markus Klein
VP, Finance | Redwood Inference

Emma / David —

Good news: Redwood Finance is prepared to approve a conditional one-time onboarding credit equal to 6% of first-year committed spend (we estimate ~$66k) subject to a few standard guardrails.

Conditions (high level):
- 24-month committed term with minimum annual usage floors (we will include numbers in the amendment).
- A list of four hospital sites you commit to move from pilot to production within 12 months.
- 50% of the credit is subject to a clawback if the usage floor is not met by month 9; repayment will be netted against invoices.
- Integration vendor fee ($20k) will be a separate pass-through in the SOW.

We're preparing a short exception memo and revised pricing attachment for signature. Can you confirm the four target hospitals and that procurement can accept the clawback mechanics? If yes, we will aim to have a signed contract and SOW in the next 7 business days to meet your board window.

Thanks — really excited to get this across the finish line.

Tessa Morgan
